findings.before: ViewSelector and FilterSelector use existing props. Store save/remove functions return promises. HTTP endpoint wrappers accept the existing payload shapes.
findings.after: Exports, props, endpoint wrappers and ordinary payload fields remain. No upper component signature change is required for the shared selectors.
findings.consequence: Cashflow_CN shared ViewSelector receives the new internals without a caller rewrite. Behavior still changes for CES role-owned items.
findings.next_action: Validate shared selector behavior for each enabled CES tile.

findings.classification: intentional CES policy hold; inspected implementation and retained controlled execution
findings.before: Role-owned writes could submit scalar moduleOwner and assigneeList under the enabled builder POC flag.
findings.after: With the role-builder flag enabled, CES/unknown mixed builder ownership disables role selection and role-owned save/remove controls. Stores reject role-owned create/update/delete before HTTP. Existing row writes with unknown ownership also reject. Known private creator-owned writes remain.
findings.consequence: CES users cannot share new views/filters by role, modify/delete role-owned records, or delete unclassified records through these shared stores. Private items work after known ownership is available.
findings.next_action: Agree the CES ownership rule before enabling role sharing. Keep server ownership metadata complete for private update/delete.

findings.classification: unchanged role-query request; migration compatibility gap; inspected implementation
findings.confidence: high for request construction; unknown backend result
findings.before: POC list queries use getUser().role as assignee and moduleOwner. Non-POC list queries use owner=user ID.
findings.after: List queries still use one scalar role; they do not query all CES roleList entries. Details are still readable by row key. Neither list nor details are blocked by the write hold.
findings.consequence: A CES-only user without a preserved trusted scalar profile can send absent role query filters. Shared-item visibility cannot be claimed equal to EMS2. Backend handling and data authorization remain unverified.
findings.owner: unknown saved-item service and application owners
findings.next_action: Agree role-query semantics and test saved-item visibility against the actual backend. Do not infer a scalar from comma-joined assignments.

findings.classification: separate unchanged creator-owned upper flow; inspected implementation
findings.confidence: high for source; unknown deployed behavior
findings.before: Cashflow advanced search calls exported raw HTTP filter APIs and supplies owner/creator ID, empty assignee and moduleOwner. Shared AdvancedSearch templates are private and creator-owned.
findings.after: This flow remains separate from the guarded FilterSelector store. It uses unchanged HTTP methods and owner-based controls.
findings.consequence: The existing creator-owned advanced-filter path needs no API migration for role multiplicity. The shared store hold is not a universal restriction on every raw HTTP consumer.
findings.next_action: Keep this flow creator-owned and include it in consumer acceptance; verify server enforcement for returned records.

findings.classification: conservative unresolved role-exclusion boundary; inspected implementation and controlled execution
findings.confidence: high for helper outputs; caller reach unknown
findings.before: SETTLEMENTS_CLIENT_DATA close/replay required scalar role != PSS_RO plus granted action.
findings.after: Those two helpers return false for a resolved CES target even when close/replay actions are granted. Other settlement subtypes still use the ordinary grant checks.
findings.consequence: An upper app calling these helpers loses these two CES client-data actions until the exclusion rule is agreed. No non-test upper caller was found in the bounded supplied repos search.
findings.next_action: Agree multi-role exclusion semantics and inspect deployed consumers before claiming action parity.

findings.classification: unchanged telemetry helper; migration-data semantic gap
findings.before: getUserProfile() extracts the scalar suffix from a user.entitlements key containing X_RATANONE.
findings.after: Its source blob is identical to baseline. It keeps the same no-argument signature and does not interpret CES assignments. MonitorUser.profile still uses it. With no legacy key, profile is empty.
findings.consequence: CES-only analytics can lose the old scalar profile label. This is a reporting difference, not an authorization grant.
findings.next_action: Decide whether analytics needs a separate CES assignment field; retain the existing scalar meaning.

findings.classification: actual upper scalar-role consumer; source-derived conditional impact
findings.confidence: high for call chain; backend outcome unknown
findings.before: EMS2 X_RATANONE roleName supplies the scalar profile for cashflow auth-limit queries.
findings.after: getUserRole() still forwards getUser().role. CES assignments alone do not supply that scalar. If no trusted legacy role is retained, checkAuthLimit embeds undefined as the profile URL segment.
findings.consequence: Single and bulk pending-verification auth-limit checks can request an undefined profile. Bulk request failure is converted to success=false/query auth limit failed. Actual server response and approval impact are unverified.
findings.owner: unknown cashflow business/profile and service owners
findings.next_action: Preserve an agreed trusted scalar data profile or define a versioned auth-limit contract before migrating these workflows. Joined CES assignments are not an established profile.

limits: Only supplied repositories and source paths were searched. No non-test external consumer of the two client-data helper names was found.
Cashflow source is an untracked filesystem checkout without its own .git. Exact file hashes bind its observed source.
Controlled Jest execution uses substituted HTTP/hooks/UI boundaries and does not establish actual server behavior.
Live saved-item visibility, authoritative profile semantics, deployed feature flags/import maps, and upper application acceptance remain unverified.

limitations: Machine source findings do not establish semantic approval or complete dictionary/grammar review.
